what.text: Glutathione is a small molecule made of three amino acids (a tripeptide). The body makes it, and it acts as an antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

src.label: Mischley et al., J Parkinsons Dis, 2017
Greenwich Rx recall notice, posted by FDA

what.text: Adonis Clinical carries glutathione as a compounded injection and as a compounded nasal spray, through Beluga. Neither form is FDA approved.
No study has tested injected or nasal glutathione for aging or longevity in people.

research.text: Human studies of injected or nasal glutathione are few and small. Most were in Parkinson's disease, where they did not show a clear benefit over placebo. Skin-lightening studies are small, and reviewers rate the IV evidence as weak. None measured aging.
Each is listed below as it was run.

research.title: IV glutathione in Parkinson's disease, 2009

facts.v: Randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind pilot, University of South Florida
21 people with Parkinson's not well controlled on their medicines: 11 glutathione, 10 placebo
IV three times a week for 4 weeks, then 8 weeks of follow-up

research.found: Well tolerated, with no withdrawals for side effects. Disease scores did not differ significantly between groups.

src.label: Hauser et al., Mov Disord, 2009

research.title: Nasal glutathione safety in Parkinson's, 2015

facts.v: Randomized, double-blind, placebo (saline) controlled, Bastyr University Research Institute, Washington
30 people with Parkinson's, split across placebo and two doses
Adverse events, blood chemistry, sinus irritation, sense of smell, compliance

research.found: No substantial differences in adverse events between groups. All groups met the tolerability criteria.

src.label: Mischley et al., Mov Disord, 2015

research.title: Nasal glutathione in Parkinson's, 2017

facts.v: 45 people with Parkinson's, Hoehn and Yahr stage 1 to 3

research.found: All groups improved, including placebo. Neither glutathione group did better than placebo. One person in the higher-dose group developed cardiomyopathy.

src.label: Mischley et al., J Parkinsons Dis, 2017

research.title: IV glutathione during heart-attack stenting, 2019

facts.v: Randomized, placebo-controlled pilot, Sapienza University of Rome
50 patients with ST-elevation heart attack having emergency angioplasty
Infusion before the procedure and at 24, 48 and 72 hours
Oxidative stress markers in blood, nitric oxide, troponin

research.found: Oxidative stress markers were lower with glutathione than placebo. The authors said a larger trial with clinical endpoints was needed.

src.label: Tanzilli et al., BMJ Open, 2019

research.text: A 2025 systematic review found only one placebo-controlled study of IV glutathione for skin lightening, with 16 people per group, and its result was not statistically significant. The reviewers concluded IV glutathione is contraindicated for this use because of lack of efficacy and side effects. A 2026 review called the IV evidence too limited to justify routine cosmetic use.

src.label: Sarkar et al., Int J Dermatol, 2025 (systematic review)
Aloraini et al., J Med Life, 2026 (review)

research.text: Glutathione's role as an antioxidant is well established in cell and animal biology. Whether injected or sprayed glutathione changes aging in people has not been studied.

src.label: Aloraini et al., J Med Life, 2026 (review)

us.text: Glutathione is not FDA approved as a medicine. It sits in FDA's 503A Category 1, the group of nominated substances still under evaluation, which pharmacies may compound under FDA's interim policy if its conditions are met. FDA has warned repeatedly about contaminated compounded glutathione injections. As of October 31, 2026.

items.text: none for glutathione as a medicine. The only FDA-approved product we found that contains a glutathione form is BSS PLUS, an eye-surgery irrigation solution (approved 1981) that contains glutathione disulfide among its salts.

items.text: FDA says it does not intend to take action against a 503A compounder for using a Category 1 substance if the conditions in its interim guidance are met.

src.label: FDA, Bulk drug substances under section 503A

items.text: FDA warned compounders on February 1, 2019 not to use glutathione powder from one repackager, labelled as a dietary supplement, for sterile injectables. Seven clinic patients had reactions within minutes of IV glutathione, and FDA's testing found excessive endotoxin, some up to five times the appropriate limit.

src.label: FDA, concerns with dietary ingredient glutathione in sterile injectables

items.text: on August 27, 2026, FDA said it knew of at least 30 patients with adverse events after IV glutathione made from dietary-supplement-grade glutathione from one supplier, some hospitalized. FDA reminded compounders not to use supplement-grade ingredients in injectables.

src.label: FDA, reminder not to use supplement-grade glutathione for injectables

items.text: compounding pharmacies have recalled glutathione injections for elevated endotoxin, including Greenwich Rx in October 2026, which reported two emergency visits after IV use of a product meant for under-the-skin injection.

src.label: Greenwich Rx recall notice, posted by FDA

items.text: FDA has said it has not approved any injectable drug for skin whitening or lightening, that such products are unapproved new drugs, and that their ingredients can include glutathione. In 2014 US Marshals seized glutathione kits sold for skin whitening at FDA's request.

us.text: Compounded drugs are not FDA approved. FDA does not review their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.

world.lead: We found no regulator that approves glutathione for aging. Australia makes injectable glutathione prescription-only. Health Canada has recalled unauthorized glutathione injections for contamination. Glutathione is not named on the WADA list.

countries.status: Not approved. 503A Category 1 (under evaluation); compounding under FDA's interim policy. FDA warnings on contaminated injections (2019, 2026).

after.title: Sport
after.text: Glutathione is not named on the 2026 WADA Prohibited List or on the 2027 list. Separately, the list prohibits intravenous infusions or injections of more than 100 mL in total per 12-hour period at all times (method M2.2), except those legitimately received in hospital treatment, surgery or clinical diagnostic investigations. That rule is about the method, whatever the substance. The 2027 list, which takes effect January 1, 2027, keeps the same rule.

side.text: In small trials, IV and nasal glutathione were generally tolerated. The main documented harm with compounded glutathione injections is contamination with endotoxin, which FDA has linked to reactions including fever, low blood pressure and hospital stays.

items.text: no withdrawals for side effects in the IV Parkinson's pilot; no excess adverse events with nasal glutathione over 3 months. One person on higher-dose nasal glutathione developed cardiomyopathy.

items.text: seven patients given IV glutathione had nausea, vomiting, lightheadedness, chills, body aches and sneezing within minutes; one had low blood pressure and trouble breathing and went to hospital. Another patient was admitted with a possible bloodstream infection.

items.text: at least 30 patients had fever, chills, pain, dizziness, signs of shock and sepsis-like symptoms after IV glutathione; some were hospitalized. FDA notes endotoxin can also cause death.

unconfirmed: We could not confirm glutathione's status with the MHRA (UK) or with the EMA and EU national regulators.
We could not reach the TGA's product register to check whether any glutathione injection is approved in Australia; we confirmed only its Schedule 4 listing.
The English page of FDA's consumer update on injectable skin lightening products returned 'page not found'; we read FDA's own Vietnamese edition, dated September 2015.
We found no human study of glutathione nasal spray outside Parkinson's disease, and none in healthy people.
surprises: Glutathione injections are widely marketed for wellness and skin lightening, but FDA says it has not approved any injectable skin-lightening drug, and a 2025 systematic review called IV glutathione contraindicated for that use.
FDA warned about endotoxin in glutathione made from supplement-grade powder in 2019 and had to warn again in August 2026 after at least 30 more patients were harmed.
In the largest nasal trial (Parkinson's, 2017), placebo improved as much as glutathione.
